I’m happy to help you stay informed! Because I don’t have direct access to live feeds right here, I’ll outline a few practical options so you can pull the most up‑to‑date stock news yourself: | Option | How It Works | Quick Example | |--------|--------------|---------------| | **Yahoo Finance RSS** | Subscribe to ticker‑specific RSS feeds (`https://finance.yahoo.com/rss/headline?s=AAPL`). Most browsers let you add them as “news” sources. | `curl https://query2.finance.yahoo.com/v10/finance/quoteSummary/AAPL` – returns JSON including headlines. | | **NewsAPI.org** | A simple REST endpoint that aggregates articles across many outlets. You can filter by keywords (“stock”, “NASDAQ”) or tickers. | ```python
import requests
url='https://newsapi.org/v2/everything'\nparams={'q':'AAPL', 'sortBy':'publishedAt','language':'en'}\nr=requests.get(url, headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer YOUR_KEY'}, params=params)\nprint(r.json()['articles'][0]['title'])``` | | **Alpha Vantage Technical & Fundamental Data** | While primarily financial metrics, their *NEWS* feed gives headline summaries tied to symbols. | `https://www.alphavantage.co/query?function=NEWS_SENTIMENT&symbol=AAPL&apikey=YOURKEY` | | **Bloomberg Terminal / Refinitiv Eikon** | If you’re in finance, those platforms deliver instant alerts, press releases, earnings calls, etc. | Use Bloomberg’s `BLOOMBERG ` → search “Stock Market News”. | ### Sample Script Using NewsAPI (Python) Below is a minimal script you can run locally once you sign up for a free key: ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Fetches the top 5 recent news stories mentioning a given ticker symbol. """ import os import sys from datetime import datetime, timedelta import requests def fetch_stock_news(symbol="AAPL", limit=5): api_key = os.getenv("NEWS_API_KEY") if not api_key: raise RuntimeError( "Please set NEWS_API_KEY environment variable with your NewsAPI token." ) url = "https://newsapi.org/v2/everything" today = datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%d") yesterday = (datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=1)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d") payload = { "q": f"\"{symbol}\" OR \"${symbol}\"", "domains": "bloomberg.com,yahoo.com,cnbc.com,reuters.com", "from": yesterday, "to": today, "sortBy": "relevancy", "pageSize": limit, "language": "en", } response = requests.get(url, headers={"X-Api-Key": api_key}, params=payload) data = response.json() if data["status"] != "ok": print(f"[ERROR] {data}") return [] results = [] for article in data["articles"]: title = article["title"] source = article["source"]["name"] published_at = article["publishedAt"].split('T')[0] link = article["url"] results.append({ "title": title, "source": source, "date": published_at, "link": link, }) return results if __name__ == "__main__": sym = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "TSLA" try: news_items = fetch_stock_news(sym) for i, item in enumerate(news_items, start=1): print(f"{i}. [{item['date']}] ({item['source']}): {item['title']}\n Link: {item['link']}\n") except Exception as exc: print(exc) ``` #### Usage ```bash export NEWS_API_KEY= python fetch_stock_news.py GOOGL ``` This will output something like: ``` 1. [2026-05-12] (Reuters): Alphabet reports Q1 revenue beats expectations... Link: https://www.reuters.com/article/alphabet-q1 ... 2. [2026-05-11] (CNBC): Google CEO announces new AI initiative... Link: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/... … ``` --- If you prefer a GUI solution, consider adding the same query to a service like **Google Alerts**, setting the alert frequency to “as-it-happens,” and filtering by keyword `"ticker"` or `"$ticker"`. That way you receive email digests whenever major coverage appears.
